stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: Urban planners in Ridgeport are studying a proposed light-rail station on Fulton Street. They selected a random sample of 250 people from a list of all Ridgeport residents who live within 1 kilometer of the proposed station site. Each person in the sample was asked whether they support or oppose building the station, and 60 people said they oppose it. Every person in the sample gave one of these two answers.
choices: Most Ridgeport residents support building the proposed light-rail station on Fulton Street.
Most Ridgeport residents within 1 kilometer of the site support building the proposed station.
Most Ridgeport residents within 1 kilometer of the site oppose building the proposed station.
Most Ridgeport residents farther than 1 kilometer from the site oppose building the station.
explanation: The sample was drawn at random from Ridgeport residents who live within 1 kilometer of the site, so the result applies only to that group. The number reported is the people who oppose the station: 60 of 250. That leaves 250 − 60 = 190 who support it, or 76%, which is a clear majority. So you can conclude that most residents within 1 kilometer of the site support the station.

A.why: You applied the result to all Ridgeport residents. Only people living within 1 kilometer of the site were sampled, and people who live farther away may feel very differently about the station.

C.why: You took the reported count of 60 as the main result. Those 60 are the people who oppose the station, and they are only 24% of the sample. The other 190 support it.

D.why: You assumed that residents who live farther away would react the opposite way. No one living more than 1 kilometer from the site was surveyed, so the data say nothing about that group.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A sports scientist studying a regional running league selected a random sample of 120 runners from the league's list of registered members who are older than 50. Of the runners in the sample, 84 reported doing strength training at least twice a week.
choices: Most of the league's registered runners do strength training at least twice a week.
Most of the league's runners aged 50 or younger do strength training less than twice a week.
Exactly 70% of the league's runners older than 50 do strength training at least twice a week.
Most of the league's runners older than 50 do strength training at least twice a week.
explanation: The sample was drawn at random from league runners older than 50, so the conclusion has to be about that group. In the sample, 84 of 120 (70%) strength train at least twice a week, which is a majority. A sample estimates the population, so the safe conclusion is that most of the league's runners older than 50 strength train at least twice a week.

A.why: You applied the result to every runner in the league. Only runners older than 50 were sampled, so the data say nothing about younger members.

B.why: You assumed that younger runners would behave the opposite way from older runners. No runners aged 50 or younger were sampled, so this was never tested.

C.why: You correctly calculated that 84 out of 120 is 70%, but you treated a sample result as an exact population value. A different random sample would probably give a slightly different percent.

Most of the program members who bought plant-based milk last month also drink cow's milk.
Most members of the grocery chain's loyalty program, whatever they buy, do not drink cow's milk.
Most of the program members who did not buy plant-based milk last month drink cow's milk.
explanation: The sampled group is loyalty-program members who bought plant-based milk last month. Of the 400 sampled, 136 said yes, so 400 − 136 = 264 (66%) said no. That is a majority, so you can conclude that most members of that group do not drink cow's milk.

B.why: You treated 136 as a majority without comparing it with half the sample. Half of 400 is 200, so 136 is a minority. Most of the people sampled said no.

C.why: You extended the result to every loyalty-program member. Only members who bought plant-based milk were sampled, and they are likely to drink less cow's milk than members in general.

D.why: You reasoned that members who didn't buy plant-based milk must behave the opposite way. That group was never sampled, so the data can't tell you anything about it.
